note: Featured targets: one-click chips. Static data in /data/<slug>/ (scripts/precompute). Positions are each target's frame centre; the expected values are from catalogues (docs/skyshift-hackathon-plan.html, demo targets table).

targets.name: Barnard's Star
targets.look_for: Steps north about 5″ each visit, under one SPHEREx pixel. Subtract two visits to see it. Its core saturates, so the shift is measured on the wings.

targets.name: Epsilon Indi B
targets.look_for: A brown-dwarf pair under 1″ apart, seen as one dot moving 2.3″ per visit. Epsilon Indi A, very bright, sits 7′ away.

targets.name: WISE 0855−0714
targets.look_for: The coldest known brown dwarf. Absent in D1–D3; in D5–D6 a dot with no Gaia ring steps west about 4″ per visit. By visit 3 it is 4″ from a Gaia star, too close to measure apart, so its spectrum and brightness stop at visit 2.

targets.name: RW Aurigae
targets.look_for: A young star that stays put while its brightness and spectrum change between visits. May saturate in the short bands.

targets.name: R Draconis
targets.look_for: A pulsating giant near the north ecliptic pole, so SPHEREx sees it many times. Watch it brighten and fade; the core saturates.

targets.name: Comet 3I/ATLAS
targets.look_for: The third known interstellar object. The frames follow the comet, so the stars stream past while it stays near the centre.

targets.name: (59) Elpis
targets.look_for: A main-belt asteroid. It crosses the field between exposures; the violet diamond marks where its known orbit puts it in each frame, so a dot sitting on the diamond is the asteroid.

targets.name: (31) Euphrosyne
targets.look_for: A large main-belt asteroid. It crosses the field between exposures; the violet diamond marks where its known orbit puts it in each frame, so a dot sitting on the diamond is the asteroid.
